subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<skill>.enabled:false` become a hard read/exec/write/sandbox deny boundary, or should it remain prompt eligibility while a separate strict skill-access policy owns hard denial?
rationale: This changes a security boundary and public config semantics across trusted personal-agent and multi-user deployments, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Define a hard disabled-skill boundary
options.body: Make disabled skills inaccessible through central policy and update read/write/edit/apply_patch, exec, sandbox materialization, UI/status, docs, and regression tests around that contract.

options.title: Add a separate strict access policy
options.body: Keep `enabled:false` as visibility/eligibility and introduce an explicit strict security mode for deployments that need disabled-skill filesystem and execution denial.

options.title: Document existing trusted-code model
options.body: Keep current behavior and clarify that operators must use sandboxing, tool policy, install policy, and filesystem controls rather than `enabled:false` for access isolation.

recommendation.title: Define a hard disabled-skill boundary
recommendation.body: Make disabled skills inaccessible through central policy and update read/write/edit/apply_patch, exec, sandbox materialization, UI/status, docs, and regression tests around that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and security/config ownership signals make steipete the best available owner for the boundary decision.
